messages:
Marie: Quick design pass — proposing a 'Cobalt' dark token set for the console. want to call out syntax weights and chart color harmonies before we lock.
Sam: Love the name. Can you paste the hexs and a quick rationale? :eyes:
Marie: Sure — primary #0f3557, accent #2fa4ff, highlight #6be1ff, muted #9fb3c8, bg #071423. Goal: richer mid-tones so charts read against bg without bright whites.
Jordan: Main concern: code blocks — current syntax uses very bright foregrounds that look harsh on cobalt. We should reduce contrast on keywords and bump comments slightly.
Lee: Agreed. On keywords I'd reduce weight from 700 -> 600 and shift color from #ffd27f to #ffb86b. Keep strings warm-ish (#9be37b) so they pop but don't clash with accent.
Marie: Here's a quick snippet of the proposed palette and token rules:

```
--bg: #071423
--panel: #0f3557
--text: #dbeefc
--muted: #9fb3c8
--accent: #2fa4ff
--highlight: #6be1ff
--keyword: #ffb86b (600)
--string: #9be37b
--comment: #7f9fb0 (italic)
```

Sam: Nice. Chart note: the line charts have overlapping hues currently. Suggest palette for charts: cyan (#6be1ff), cobalt (#2fa4ff), teal (#2fd6a1), warm orange (#ffb86b), mauve (#c39bff).
Jordan: Also propose discrete colorblind-safe variant for charts (darker contrasts, shape markers), and ensure legend text meets 4.5:1 for normal text.
Lee: For syntax weights: can we try keyword 600, fn name 700, variable 500, builtin 600, number 600, comment 400? Comments should stay legible but not attention-grabbing.
Kai: Copy nit — the theme toggle label currently says "Dark (Cobalt)" — maybe "Cobalt dark" or "Cobalt theme"? Also add small accessibility hint under theme settings: "Recommended for low-light environments; adjust contrast in Accessibility settings." Could be truncated.
Marie: I prefer 'Cobalt (dark)' — keeps style consistent with 'Aurora (light)'. But happy to adjust if product wants shorter.
Sam: UX question: should we expose a "high-contrast" toggle that switches to a more extreme palette? That avoids changing defaults for everyone.
Jordan: Yes, high-contrast toggle is better. When on, swap text -> #ffffff and panel -> #041826, increase stroke widths on charts, and enable outline focus ring 3px.
Lee: Accessibility testing plan: run 6 permutations (default, high-contrast) x (charts with lines/areas) x (code examples). I'll put together a small QA checklist.
Marie: Putting together a quick prototype in Figma — will link in a follow-up. For now, attaching an example of a code snippet render we ran on v3 (screenshot): https://figma.redwood/proto/COBALT-123 :sparkles:
DesignBot: Reminder — design token update will create a migration PR for components and docs. ETA: 2 days.
Kai: One more copy thought — toggle tooltip: "Switch theme. Tip: High-contrast mode boosts readability for low-vision users." Shorten to "boosts readability for low-vision users"?
Sam: Fine by me.
Marie: Thanks all — I'll post the Figma link and the test checklist once ready. If no objections by EOD we'll move this to a branch.
Lee: No objections from me. +1 :thumbsup:
Jordan: +1 for the syntax weight changes. Will validate in storybook.
Kai: +1 for copy tweak.
Sam: +1 on palette. Great work.
Marie: Cool — merging direction. Will file the PR and tag @eng-frontend and @a11y for review.
